message_mismatch: Speed mismatch — selected components do not share the same speed count: {details}.
_note: Crankset included so it gets a verdict badge — a 1x12 crank with an 11s drivetrain is a real mismatch.

message_match: Shifter and rear derailleur both use {value} actuation.
message_mismatch: Actuation mismatch — shifter and rear derailleur use different technologies: {details}. A mechanical shifter cannot drive a wireless/electronic derailleur (and vice versa).
_note: groupsets.json technology values seen so far: 'mechanical', 'wireless'. Future: 'electronic-wired' (Di2). The check is exact-string equality.

message_match: Rear derailleur and chain agree on the SRAM Flattop standard.
message_mismatch: SRAM Transmission/Flattop mismatch — {details}. SRAM T-Type Transmission derailleurs require a Flattop chain; classic SRAM Eagle derailleurs require a non-Flattop chain.
_note: Flattop detection: groupsets.json compatible_chains string contains 'Flattop'. Covers both T-Type Transmission (Eagle 90/X0/XX/XX SL) and SRAM Road AXS (which also uses Flattop).

message_match: Shifter and rear derailleur are from the same brand ({value}) — cable pull / wireless protocol consistent.
message_mismatch: Brand mismatch — {details}. Shimano and SRAM shifters and rear derailleurs use different cable pull ratios (Dyna-Sys / HG+ vs Eagle Exact Actuation) or wireless protocols (Di2 vs AXS). They cannot drive each other across brands.
_note: Cross-brand shifter↔RD is always incompatible. Other role-pairs (chain↔cassette, chain↔crankset) are NOT covered here — they have legitimate caveat cases (e.g. SRAM chain on Shimano cassette functions but lacks HG+ chamfering) handled by explicit caveat rules.
